findings.title: Retry cleanup can delete successfully scheduled reminders
findings.body: The retry-limit branch does not require scheduled=false. Two overlapping cron invocations can both fetch an unscheduled reminder with retryCount=1: one fails and stores 2, while the other succeeds and marks it scheduled without resetting the counter. The next cron run then deletes this successfully scheduled reminder before its scheduled date. Twilio still has the queued SMS, but its local reference is lost, preventing subsequent cancellation or rescheduling through that reminder. Restrict retry-based cleanup to unscheduled SMS reminders.

findings.title: Failure bookkeeping can abort the entire reminder batch
findings.body: The update inside the catch block can itself throw, escaping the per-reminder error handling. For example, another cron invocation can delete a reminder after this invocation fetched it because its date has passed or its retry count reached the limit. Updating that missing row throws, and the catch block attempts to update the same missing row again. The resulting uncaught error stops processing all remaining reminders and returns an error for the whole job. Make failure recording tolerate missing rows and handle bookkeeping errors without terminating the batch.

findings.title: Increment retry counts atomically to avoid losing failed attempts
findings.body: Both failure paths assign reminder.retryCount + 1 using the snapshot fetched before processing the batch. If two cron invocations overlap and both read retryCount=0, their failed scheduling attempts both write 1. Two failures therefore leave the reminder below the deletion threshold, allowing additional scheduling attempts despite the intended two-failure limit. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths rather than overwriting the counter from the fetched value.
